title: Total mass of the doubly-conditioned hard distribution
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and work on the finite sample space of hard samples on $n$ coordinates, equipped with its ambient counting measure. Let $\mu$ be the measure obtained by conditioning this counting measure first on the disjointness event—that Alice's input set and Bob's input set are disjoint—and then on the event that Bob's bit at the special coordinate equals $\mathrm{false}$. Then $\mu$ is a probability measure; equivalently, $\mu$ assigns total mass $1$ to the whole sample space.
replaced: Conditioning the disjoint law on $Y_{T} = false$ gives a probability measure.
